summary: All four editions agree on the core fact: Soviet partisans killed Polish civilians in Naliboki. However, EN and IT are closely aligned, providing a precise date (8 May 1943), casualty estimate (127 or 128), and geopolitical context (German-occupied Poland, now Belarus). RU provides a slightly different casualty figure (129) with demographic detail (three women, several teenagers) and adds geographic specificity (Naliboki forest), while omitting the German occupation context. PL's lead is the most minimal, omitting the date, precise casualty numbers, and occupation context, and refers to Naliboki as a village rather than a town.
